note: Re-judged 2026-10-24 (independent auditor, authored none of 9c3697d0d1). RFC 7606 Section 7.16, New Text: "An UPDATE message with a malformed ATTR_SET attribute SHALL be handled using the approach of "treat as withdraw"." The only change to TestRFC7606AttrSetMalformedInnerAttributes is the call, now ValidateUpdateRFC7606Peer(..., asn4, nil, false, false); no input or assertion changed. Its cases assert exact TreatAsWithdraw with AttrCode 128 for a 2-octet inner AGGREGATOR, an inner ORIGIN flag conflict and an inner NEXT_HOP framing overrun, and exact None for the conforming counterparts, under both outer ASN widths. Producer at HEAD: validateAttrSetDepth judges included attributes with validateAttribute(..., true, true, receivePolicy{}), so the receiving peer's as-set accept never reaches them (stated in the validateAttrSetAttr comment). FINDING (not verdict-changing, carried and sharpened): with receivePolicy{} an AS_SET in an included AS_PATH makes the ATTR_SET malformed through the RFC 9774 set scan, yet RFC 9774 never calls an AS_SET malformed and never mentions ATTR_SET, and RFC 6368 Section 5 makes ATTR_SET malformed only when "The included attributes are malformed themselves." No test pins that reading either way. Fix: decide the reading from FRR and BIRD source, then either run the inner AS_PATH validator with the set scan off or keep it, and in both cases add a tagged case asserting the chosen exact action for an inner AS_SET. Unit ran green at HEAD.
